mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 7.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when UNRATE exceeds 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of below-trend GDP growth (GDPC1 < 15500) and elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 230) signals stagflationary pressures, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when both GDPC1 < 15500 and CPIAUCSL > 230.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, a decline in housing starts (HOUST < 900) signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when HOUST < 900 and the economy is in a late-cycle expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 98.0 signals weakening supply chain activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when INDPRO < 98.0.

mechanism_narrative: A strong labor market (PAYEMS growth) signals robust corporate hiring and earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when PAYEMS is above its 12-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 230) and high unemployment (UNRATE > 7.0) signals stagflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of the periods when both CPIAUCSL > 230 and UNRATE > 7.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer spending (RSAFS) signals robust economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of the periods when RSAFS is above its 12-month average.
